feasibility_reasoning:
(a) The 874-element recalc is not caused by --sticky-header-h being inherited. On the real fixture page, any change to <html>'s computed style recalcs the whole document. Probes after hydration at 1x: html.style.scrollPaddingTop -> 918-926 elements; a <style>html{...} rule -> 918; the +3px variable write -> 918 even with `@property inherits:false` injected (registration confirmed: body reads 96px, html 107px). The only cheap case is an attribute on html with no matching rule (1 element). In 4x CDP traces with the H5(a) CSS injected, the recalc is still there: B-1 874 el / 268 ms, B-2 874 / 212 ms, B-inv 882 / 345 ms, same invalidation (inline style on HTML, stack S index 422:14673 = Header.tsx:566). Control C, which suppresses the html write, removes it. The decisive lines are Header.tsx:566, root.style.setProperty, which must not run at load.
(a) also changes anchor offsets. Today styles.css:6678-6680 scroll-padding and :6681-6683 [id] scroll-margin add up: a Chromium probe lands the target at 254 px = 127+127. Dropping [id]'s use of the variable halves native/router hash offsets (router-core scroll-restoration.js:184 scrollIntoView; ClubHubHero.tsx:241, EventAgendaBoardView.tsx:122, ExpertMaterialsExplorer.tsx:106), so the risk note's "identical offsets" is violated. No e2e anchor test exists.
(b) The forced Layout in the hydration task comes from `document.fonts?.ready` at Header.tsx:516 (stack index 422:14025). It flushes the --hdr-* writes from measure() (422:13541), and costs 3-14 ms at 4x. Mount getBoundingClientRect reads cost 0.1-0.3 ms (el=1). The "138 ms" figure is the effect's inclusive time, not avoidable layout.
Tests: Header.test.tsx:1316-1324 and 1427-1437 assert synchronous publication at mount, and ControlledResizeObserver.fire (:430-432) passes [] entries. No bundle/chunk/SSR/noHasSelectors impact.
blocking_issues: (a) @property inherits:false does not prevent the full-document recalc on this page. Any computed-style change on <html> (even plain scroll-padding-top or a <style> html rule) recalcs ~920 elements. Measured: B traces still show 874-882 el / 212-345 ms at 4x.
(a) Removing var() from [id] scroll-margin halves native anchor offsets (254 -> 127 px; the two properties add up today), which contradicts the 'offsets identical' requirement. No e2e gate covers it.
(b) Misattribution: the forced layout in hydration is document.fonts.ready (Header.tsx:516), not getBoundingClientRect. The mount gBCR reads cost <0.3 ms.

(b) Under Lantern, removing the only Layout from the ~96 ms (1x) hydration task flips its multiplier from x2 to x4 (Simulator.js:239). Mobile TBT rises by ~+190 ms, desktop by +41 ms (sandbox) to ~+136 ms (PSI host).
Header.test.tsx:1316-1324 and 1427-1471 assert synchronous mount publication, and the RO test double passes empty entries. Both need a rewrite.
effect_reasoning:
Lantern applies x0.5 of the CPU multiplier to any task that contains a Layout (trace_engine Simulator.js:239, DEFAULT_LAYOUT_TASK_MULTIPLIER 0.5).
Mobile: in the observed LH trace (lha1-mobile), the post-hydration frame task is 40.4 ms (ULT 781 el + Layout 0.2). It is simulated at 40.4 x 2 = 81 ms, which is exactly the long task index-DPN2YAij.js@6606+81, so it contributes 81 - 50 = 31 ms TBT. The baseline2 index-attributed tasks of 119/69/68 ms give 69/19/18 ms. The claimed 137-177 ms comes from CDP 4x DevTools throttling, which Lantern does not score.
Desktop (lha1-desktop): the frame task is 35.1 ms, simulated at x0.5 = 17.5 ms, so 0 TBT. On a ~3x slower PSI host it is 105 x 0.5 = 53, about 3 ms. Under the sandbox planning rule it is 70, about 20 ms.
As specified, (a) saves about 0: the recalc survives in the 4x traces. A canonical-harness what-if gave DELTA TBT +6 ms and score ±0 (noise-dominated, n=2).
(b) is likely net negative. The root hydration task (95.6 ms at 1x) is scored at x2 (vendor-react@6415+191 = 95.6 x 2) only because of the fonts.ready-forced Layout. Remove it and the task is scored at 382 ms, about +190 ms mobile TBT and +41..+136 ms desktop.
Cheaper option that works: do not write html's style at load. Skip the mount publication when the measured height is near the CSS default, or use per-breakpoint constants. Control C removed the recalc completely. Its value is bounded by the 31 ms computed above.
corrected_estimate: H5 as specified: mobile TBT about 0 for (a), plus roughly +190 ms (worse) if (b) removes the last Layout from the hydration task; desktop about 0 for (a), +41..+136 ms for (b). Do not ship (b). The working alternative is to skip or suppress the --sticky-header-h write to <html> at load (Header.tsx:548-585, styles.css:6678-6683) and keep measure() and document.fonts.ready unchanged. Its effect: mobile TBT -16..-31 ms (one 66-81 ms simulated task becomes <50 ms), about +0.4..+0.8 points. Desktop TBT 0..-20 ms (0 on real LH desktop; about 3 ms on a slow PSI host; 20 ms under the sandbox x4 rule), about 0..+0.4 points. Under 4x CDP the style work drops by 150-340 ms, which does not count toward the score. Effort XS. The native anchor offset change (currently doubled) needs an explicit decision.
better_alternative: Do not change <html>'s computed style during load. In the sticky effect, initialise `last` from the CSS fallback and skip the write when |height - default| < ~16 px. Set the per-breakpoint CSS defaults to real header heights (fixture mobile 107 px). Alternatively, replace the runtime variable with per-breakpoint constants for html scroll-padding-top, and drop the duplicated [id] scroll-margin as a deliberate offset fix. Publish only on a real resize/settle. Keep measure()'s sync write and document.fonts.ready, so the hydration task keeps its Layout (Lantern x2). Verified by control trace C: the 874-element recalc disappears.
